prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin across all change types; at least 2 tests of a kind are required to establish a rule.
Evidence is still thin for adoption new_screen changes (only 1 test, which performed worse at -4.1% after noise correction).
Evidence is still thin for finish new_screen changes (only 1 test, which showed no clear effect at +1.4% after noise correction).
Evidence is still thin for sign_in reorder changes (only 1 test, which showed no clear effect at -0.4% after noise correction).
Predictions were consistently too high across all change types compared to noise-corrected measurements.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_screen: -4.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -0.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] Story Screen Hero Animation Redesign: Redesign the story introduction with a split screen layout featuring an animated pet preview to engage users before path selection. (why: Choose path takes a long median time (8s) with a 23.8% drop off; a visual split redesign clarifies the desktop pet concept early.)
1: [home, new_flow] Desktop Visibility Status Checker Flow: Add a setup diagnostic screen prior to pet spawning to verify screen display permissions and ensure the pet overlay renders correctly. (why: Support received 3 emails about pets not appearing on desktop, while home step has a high mean duration (2336s).)
2: [finish, redesign] Pet Care Basics Control Card Redesign: Redesign the home introduction screen into a structured two-column layout highlighting core pet controls and shortcuts. (why: Finish step drops 35.2% of users and support receives inquiries on how to hide, control, or interact with pets after onboarding.)
3: [sign_in, copy] Multi Device Account Warning Copy: Update sign-in screen headline and body text to remind users to sign in with their existing account to restore saved pets. (why: Support logged 8 complaints regarding lost or reset pets when users sign in using a different authentication method.)
4: [home, wait_info] Desktop Summoning Progress Waiting Tips: Add an interactive tip carousel and estimated time indicator to the waiting screen while the pet engine initializes. (why: Home waiting duration has a long mean of 2336s and 18.7% drop-off; active progress feedback keeps users engaged.)
5: [home, notification] Desktop Arrival Sound Notification: Enable desktop completion notification with sound effect on the waiting screen when pet loading completes. (why: Users wait median 201s on home screen and often switch away; audio and system notification alerts them when ready.)
6: [finish, hint] Desktop Tray Icon Interaction Hint: Add an illustrated hint on the final screen showing how to manage pet visibility via system tray menu. (why: 3 support tickets involved confusion over how to hide or summon pets after completing setup.)

scores.note: Choose path has a 23.8% drop-off but no support tickets were logged. Requires custom UI work.
Funnel and 3 emails point to permission issues, but adding extra flow screens historically performs poorly.
Finish step loses 35.2% of users and support reports control confusion; UI layout redesign moderate cost.
Sign-in drops 27.1% and has the highest complaint volume (8 emails); simple copy/config change with low risk.
Home step has long wait duration, but evidence relies solely on funnel data without support ticket backing.
Addresses median 201s idle wait via system notification; low implementation cost.
Finish step drops 35.2% and 3 tickets complain about pet management; simple hint addition with fast delivery.
